routeWhy: This route runs as a one-way loop: north to the volcano, west over Lake Arenal to the cloud forest, down to the Pacific, south along the coast, then a straight run back to San José. Nothing is backtracked. It puts the misty highlands early, when you have the most energy for hikes, and saves beach and moped days for the end. The Costanera coast road between Quepos and Uvita is the easiest stretch of the trip for a scooter. Every leg is 4–5 hours or less, and the La Fortuna → Monteverde leg crosses the lake by boat, which turns a travel day into a sightseeing day. Flying in and out of SJO (not LIR) keeps the first and last nights 10 minutes from the airport.

options.note: One or two stops (usually via CLT or MIA on American). Recent cheapest round trip is about $320, and the typical range is $354–537. $380 is a padded planning number because May 2027 fares are not on sale yet. It is also the closest airport to Utica (about 1 hour).

Cheapest fare: $199–290, including JetBlue nonstop from about $282. You then have to get from Utica to JFK and back: roughly 4–5 hours each way by bus or train, an estimated $60–100 round trip per person, and possibly a hotel night. Total is about $350–390 per person, so it barely beats SYR.
Round trip from $351–386, and no nonstop. LIR is in Guanacaste, about 3+ hours from La Fortuna, so this route works better for a north-Pacific beach plan than for this one.

alcohol.ageNote: The legal drinking age in Costa Rica is 18. Carry a passport photo or copy, since bars may ask for ID.

moped.dailyRateNote: 150cc street scooter in Manuel Antonio: $51/day (Dec–May), $57/day (Jun–Nov). It fits a maximum of 2 people.
moped.insuranceNote: Basic third-party insurance is usually included. Optional collision cover (CDW) is about $10/day (ESTIMATE). It caps what you can lose at the deposit.
moped.gasNote: A 125–150cc scooter needs about 2–4 L for a day of beach-hopping (ESTIMATE).
moped.deposit: $100–450, refundable, usually held on a credit card in the rider's name. It is not counted in the total.
moped.weekly: Multi-day packages exist (e.g. MangoScoot from $137 per group for multi-day 150cc off-road scooters). Ask for a 3-day rate.
moped.atv: Self-drive ATV rental is rare. Guided ATV tours run $85–158 per person (FourTrax from $110 single or $140 for 2 sharing, plus 13% tax; MidWorld about $95). ATV is listed under Activities.
rules: Bring your US driver's license and passport. Tourists can drive on a valid foreign license during their tourist stay. Rental requirements vary: some want a car license (category B) plus age 21–25, while others want a motorcycle (A or A1) endorsement. Ask your shop in writing.
If you have no motorcycle endorsement, your travel insurance may refuse to pay for a scooter crash. Read the policy's motorcycle clause before you ride.
Helmets are mandatory for rider and passenger. Make sure the shop gives you two that actually fit.
Ride in daylight only. May afternoons bring downpours, potholes and unlit roads.
Two people maximum on one scooter. Keep your pace slow on gravel.

moped.safetyNote: ⚠️ Safety first: road crashes are among the most common ways tourists get hurt in Costa Rica. Only rent if one of you is a confident two-wheel rider. Wear helmets and closed shoes, never ride after drinking (the guaro waits until you park), avoid night riding, and photograph the scooter before you take it. If you're unsure, a $5 local bus or a taxi is cheaper than a hospital.

hacks.title: Eat at sodas, not tourist restaurants
hacks.text: A casado (rice, beans, salad, plantain, protein) costs $5–9 at a soda. That's about half the price of a tourist-strip plate, and you'll be full until dinner.

hacks.title: Shop at Palí / Maxi Palí
hacks.text: Palí is Costa Rica's cheapest supermarket chain, and Auto Mercado is the most expensive. Buy local brands; imported goods are taxed heavily.

hacks.title: Pre-game with supermarket Imperial
hacks.text: A supermarket beer costs about ₡960 ($1.75–2) against $2.50–4 at a bar. Hunt for 2-for-1 happy hours at sunset.

hacks.title: Take public buses on the easy legs
hacks.text: San José → La Fortuna costs about ₡3,500 by bus against about $55 by shuttle, which saves around $95 for two. Carry small colones bills.

hacks.title: Bring your student ID
hacks.text: The Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve charges students about $12–13 instead of $25–26. Always ask about student prices.

hacks.title: Do the free stuff
hacks.text: Costa Rican beaches are public by law. Playa Espadilla, Playa Biesanz, Dominical sunsets and the El Salto swimming hole in La Fortuna all cost $0.

hacks.title: Use bank ATMs (BCR / Banco Nacional)
hacks.text: BAC charges $7.80 on foreign cards, while BCR and Banco Nacional were reported free. A no-foreign-fee debit card such as Schwab or a fintech card saves even more.

hacks.title: Don't double tip
hacks.text: Restaurant bills already include a 10% service charge plus 13% tax. Read the receipt before adding more.

hacks.title: Bring sunscreen and bug spray from home
hacks.text: Imported toiletries cost much more in Costa Rica. Pack a reef-safe sunscreen and DEET from the US.

hacks.title: Book tours direct and ask for a combo
hacks.text: Reseller prices for the same tour vary by $20–40. Operators often discount combos (e.g. Pure Trek canyoning + zipline) and pay-in-cash deals. Green season can also mean promo rates.
